# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 7 (Bu-Vb Pc7)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc7  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 7  
**Title (English, from literature):** Teaching a woman alone  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Dhammadesanā* ("Teaching a woman alone") is the seventh training rule in the *Pācittiya* chapter of the Pali *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. The rule stipulates that a Buddhist monk who teaches more than six sentences of the word of the Buddha to a woman without an informed companion must confess the offense as an expiation (*pācittiya*). The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

The rule corresponds to Pācittiya 7 in the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Bhikkhu Parivāra*, and it possesses extensive parallels across all major early Buddhist monastic traditions, including Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya prātimokṣa and vibhaṅga texts preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan. Parallel disciplinary injunctions are likewise found in nuns' lineages, such as Pali *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* and *Pātimokkha* Pācittiya 103 and their Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, and Mūlasarvāstivāda counterparts.
